feedback: Written before this robot has raced. Iterations 0 to 2 show the sensor array is not the limit: widening the span from ±0.02 to ±0.03 m, enlarging the footprint from 12 to 16 mm and moving the lead from 0.05 to 0.04 m changed max_error by under 0.001 m, and every track still ends with one line-loss event and steering_oscillation between 0.07 and 0.15. The robot drifts off the tape steadily, so I built this package to test turning authority. I kept your iteration 2 sensor array and kept the controller unchanged, so any score change comes from mass, body_length and wheel_track. Interpret the next race as follows. If line_loss_events falls below 1 and max_error drops below 0.06 on the s-bend and slalom (the expected result for this geometry), keep the narrow track and move to speed. If the robot holds the line but completion_time stays above 3.0 s, the limit is speed, so change wheel_radius. If max_error stays at 0.061 to 0.069 with line loss unchanged, turning authority is not the limit and I will revisit the footprint and speed. If steering_oscillation rises above 0.15, the narrower track has raised turn rate too far, and I will fix that in the controller before changing geometry again.
requested_changes: If the next race holds the line (line_loss_events 0 or 1 with max_error below 0.06) but completion_time stays above 3.0 s, raise wheel_radius from 0.03 to 0.035 m. Iterations 0 to 2 show progress stuck at 0.10 to 0.15 with no completions, so speed is the next limit once the line is held.

If line_loss_events and max_error are still at iteration 2 levels (1 event, 0.061 to 0.069 m) with steering_oscillation low, narrow wheel_track further from 0.10 to 0.09 m. This tests whether turn rate per unit PWM is still limiting, since the 0.12 to 0.10 m change alone is not yet shown to be enough.

If steering_oscillation rises above the 0.07 to 0.15 range seen in iterations 0 to 2, keep wheel_track at 0.10 m and reduce mass further to 0.45 kg. Lower yaw inertia reduces overshoot from the higher turn rate without giving up turning authority.
